subject: POC kickoff & hands-on working session — sample data and calendar slots
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>
Date: 2026-02-10T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: POC kickoff week of Feb 16 — sample payloads and agenda

Hi Marissa,

Hope you're well. We're excited to get the Redwood POC kicked off. We'd like to schedule a hands-on working session the week of Feb 16 to:
- review prompt sets and expected outputs
- validate routing behavior for our multi-tenant flows
- run some light load tests to validate latency under typical QPS

Can you share available slots that week? Also, can you confirm what sample payload format you need and any redaction guidance? We'll aim to share a sanitized dataset before the session.

Participants from our side: Alex Johnson (PM), Priya Sharma (Data Lead), Jake Miller (SRE).

Thanks,
Alex
Product Manager, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-02-10T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff week of Feb 16 — sample payloads and agenda

Hi Alex & team,

Great — we'd love to run that. Available slots next week (all PT):
- Tue 2026-02-17, 10:00 - 11:30
- Tue 2026-02-17, 13:00 - 14:30
- Wed 2026-02-18, 09:00 - 10:30

For the working session, our ideal deliverables before the meeting are:
1) Sample payloads (CSV or JSONL) with up to ~1k rows of typical requests; include a small set of longer sequences (~2-3% of rows) so we can validate KV cache behaviors.
2) A short list of "test prompts" you want to prioritize (5-10 prompts).
3) Any routing rules you'd like to validate (e.g., route by customer_id, priority flag).

I've attached our redaction_guidelines.pdf and a sample_payloads.csv template to this email. Priyom (SE) and Aditya (SRE/Engr-prep) are looped in to help with load test configs and prompt tuning during the session.

Which slot works for you? Once we confirm, I'll send a calendar invite and a short mutual action plan.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>, Jake Miller <jake.miller@acme.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-02-11T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff week of Feb 16 — sample payloads and agenda

Thanks Marissa. Tue 2026-02-17 works for us but can we shift to 11:00 - 12:30 PT instead of 10? The product team has a hard conflict at 10.

Per your checklist: we'd like to upload a sanitized dataset by EOD tomorrow. I've also attached an initial_test_prompts.txt with the 8 prompts we'd like to prioritize. We will ensure PII is redacted per your guidelines, but one question: do you need a mapping file that indicates which fields were redacted and how (e.g., replaced with [REDACTED] or hashed)?

Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-02-11T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff week of Feb 16 — sample payloads and agenda

Thanks — 11:00 - 12:30 PT on Tue 2026-02-17 is fine, I'll send the calendar invite now.

Short answers: a mapping file that documents which fields were redacted and the method (mask vs. hash) is very helpful for our eval team, but not strictly required if you'd rather avoid metadata that references original values. Replacing PII with [REDACTED] in the payloads + a simple schema doc is sufficient.

Agenda for the working session (draft):
- 11:00 - 11:10: Introductions & goals
- 11:10 - 11:35: Prompt review and expected outputs (Priyom + Alex)
- 11:35 - 12:00: Routing & model selection discussion (Aditya + Vivek)
- 12:00 - 12:20: Load test plan and smoke runs (SRE & Eng)
- 12:20 - 12:30: Next steps & mutual action plan

I've attached a mutual_action_plan.xlsx with proposed owners/acceptance criteria. Also: for load tests, can you confirm expected steady-state QPS and number of concurrent clients? That will determine the test harness we recommend.

Invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=acme-poc-kickoff-20260217-11am (sent)

Cheers,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-02-12T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: POC kickoff & sample data logistics

Quick follow-up ahead of Tue: a few items so we can prep staging + test harness.
1) Max sequence length we should expect? (tokenized length) If you don't know precisely, a 1k-token max is fine and we'd like ~20 examples near that length.
2) Sample size: if you can provide ~500-1k typical rows that'd be ideal.
3) Load test target: please confirm steady-state QPS and target burst QPS. For a smoke run we do 50-100 QPS; if you'd like to validate 500 QPS+, we plan a staged ramp with a short soak (2-5 minutes) per step.
4) Redaction mapping: if you provide a separate mapping.csv that notes which field was redacted (column name + method), we'll keep that internal to the eval team and delete after the POC. That's our preference but not mandatory.

If you can reply to these points or drop the files into the Drive link Marissa shared, we'll prep the test harness and a short checklist for Tue.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

- acme_poc_sample_payloads.jsonl (sanitized, PII replaced with [REDACTED])

See you on Tue at 11:00 PT — looking forward to the working session.

Best,
Alex
